newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases, market very low.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases, market very low.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index continued downwards shedding 1.67 points to close at 3448.92 in very sluggish trading, brokers said on Thursday.
"All is not well," a senior broker told Reuters. "The market is very low and we could be looking at a very gloomy six months."
Turnover was posted at 12.1 million shares traded on 366,061 shares compared to 19.479 million shillings on 430,905 shares on Wednesday.
A bourse official described Thursday's trading as flat throughout, characterised by retail trading in small deals.

Political unrest last week sparked by opposition calls for constitutional reforms jarred the market, sending it to an all-year low on Monday. The violent protests upset investors and have made many wary of this emerging market.

Nine people were killed last week in the most violent clashes between police and protesters since a campaign in July 1990 that helped persuade President Daniel arap Moi to allow a switch to multi-party politics.
Brokers said foreign investors were no longer buying aggressively on the Nairobi bourse and said they had in fact suspended or cancelled their orders.
"I do not think they will come until after elections," one broker said.
Kenya Commercial Bank was unchanged at 102, while Barclays Bank closed at 110 unchanged. Standard Chartered Bank was unchanged at 50.50.
Kenya Airways eased to 7.40 from 7.60 while Uchumi Supermarket edged to close at 37.50 from 37.25.
Kenya Power & Lighting traded at 175 from 174 while Kenya Breweries was unchanged at 57.
Foreign investors traded 2,800 shares of National Industrial Credit at 53.50 from 55 and Firestone East Africa at 28.50 from 28.

The third issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded 50,000 shillings at 101.5309 percent compared to 101.1770 percent while the fourth issue traded at 101.3430 percent from 101.8084 percent.
